title: MemDev-Bench: Does Memory Help Code Agents?Benchmarking Memory Systems over Real Repository Histories
abstract: arXiv:2610.27524v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code agents increasingly work on evolving real repositories, and memory systems aim to help them reuse earlier experience. However, such experience is diverse and evolving, so it remains unclear how memory systems organize it and thereby affect code agents. Existing benchmarks cannot answer this reliably because they lack either temporally valid histories or control over prior-task relevance. In this paper, we present MemDev-Bench to evaluate how memory systems affect code agents over diverse repository histories. It pairs each task with relevance-annotated earlier tasks from the same repository to build histories with controlled relevance. We also build an automated pipeline that reliably makes these earlier tasks executable and verifiable, producing 4,869 historical tasks for 555 base tasks. translated_title: MemDev-Bench：记忆能否帮助代码智能体？基于真实仓库历史的记忆系统基准测试
translated_abstract: 代码智能体日益在不断演化的真实仓库上工作，而记忆系统旨在帮助它们复用先前的经验。然而，这些经验是多样且不断演变的，因此记忆系统如何组织这些经验、进而如何影响代码智能体，目前仍不明确。现有基准无法可靠地回答这一问题，因为它们要么缺乏时序上有效的历史，要么无法控制先前任务的相关性。本文提出 MemDev-Bench，用于评估记忆系统在多样化仓库历史中对代码智能体的影响。该基准将每个任务与来自同一仓库、带相关性标注的早期任务配对，从而构建具有可控相关性的历史。我们还构建了一条自动化流水线，能够可靠地使这些早期任务可执行且可验证，最终为555个基础任务生成了4,869个历史任务。基于 MemDev-Bench，我们在多种开发场景下对记忆系统进行了系统性评估，得出三个主要发现。（1）记忆主……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出首个基于真实仓库历史、具有可控任务相关性的记忆系统基准 MemDev-Bench，通过自动化流水线构建了4,869个可执行可验证的历史任务，用以系统评估记忆系统对代码智能体的实际影响。
en_tdlr: MemDev-Bench is the first benchmark to systematically evaluate how memory systems affect code agents, using relevance-controlled, executable historical tasks (4,869 tasks for 555 base tasks) automatically derived from real repository histories.
